text:
Maya Patel: Quick heads-up — NovaRetail wants a short technical pilot (2 weeks) to validate RAG for order support. They asked for: baseline prompt set, eval plan, success criteria, and answers for pricing + security questionnaire. Can SEs help inventory prompts and give rough token/latency cost estimates? kickoff target: Monday.

Samir Gupta: I can take the prompt inventory. Want to break it into 3 buckets: customer-facing responses, internal agent prompts (ops), and fallback / escalation.

Riley Chen: @Maya @Samir sounds good. For cost estimates we'll need expected average turn length + concurrency. Do we have traffic profile from them?

Maya Patel: No hard numbers yet — initial ask was ~200 queries/day, peak ~10 rps during flash. We'll assume avg 80 tokens in + 120 tokens out for baseline.

Alyssa Morales: For success criteria I propose: 1) Coverage: 90% of top-50 customer intents handled without escalation; 2) Latency: 95th pct < 600ms on Hosted API; 3) Quality: human eval score >= 4/5 on 200-sample eval set. Thoughts?

Jordan Lee: All sensible. For latency SLO we should call out model variant (e.g., opt-ollama or redwood-verif-7b-quant). If they need enterprise SLA we should recommend Dedicated.

Samir Gupta: Inventory first pass — sending sample prompts below. Will add more after convo with NovaRetail PM.

Samir Gupta: ```
# Customer-facing prompts (examples)
1) "You are an order assistant. Given order id 12345, summarize status and next steps."
2) "Customer: My delivery is late. Ask clarifying Qs and propose refund policy based on order date."

# Internal agent prompts
1) "Agent helper: Suggest concise action items for ops team to resolve inventory mismatch."

# Fallback prompts
1) "If unsure, reply with: 'I don't have that info. I'll escalate to a human agent and you should receive an update within 2 hours.'"
```

Riley Chen: Nice. Using Maya's traffic estimates and avg token counts: cost ballpark (hosted) = tokens_in+out * token_price * volume. With our hosted price assumption of $0.002 / 1k tokens (example), daily cost ~ ((80+120)=200 tokens) * 200 queries = 40k tokens/day => $0.08/day. Peak latency estimate depends on model; 7b quant on GPU should hit ~200-400ms per token step, overall ~200-600ms. These are rough.

Maya Patel: Good to have a quick number to share. They will also ask about data retention and SOC controls in security Q. Can we prepare standard answers for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private?

Alyssa Morales: I'll draft canned security responses: data retention defaults (30 days ephemeral logs), option for no-retention on Dedicated, KMS/HSM integration for Private, and SOC2 + ISO certs. Share with legal before sending.

Jordan Lee: Also flag regulatory requirement: if they need EU data residency, recommend deploying to eu-west region or Private.

Samir Gupta: Next steps proposal:
- Monday kickoff w/ NovaRetail PM (30m) to capture success metrics + traffic samples
- Wed: SE delivers baseline prompt inventory (30-40 prompts) + eval set (200 samples)
- Thu: Engineering provides cost & latency estimate + recommended model variants
- End of week: draft answers for security questionnaire + optional Dedicated sizing

Maya Patel: Timeline looks good. Can @Riley and @Alyssa commit to Wed/Thu deliverables?

Riley Chen: Yep — I'll do the cost/latency note Thu morning.

Alyssa Morales: I'll draft the security write-up Tue night and loop in Legal Wed.

Samir Gupta: I'll start populating the prompt inventory today and tag intents — will push a spreadsheet to the channel when ready.

Maya Patel: Perfect. For the eval plan, Samir can you include a short rubric (correctness, helpfulness, hallucination) and a pass threshold per intent? We want an automated eval harness later.

Samir Gupta: Yep. Quick rubric notes:
- Correctness (binary)
- Helpfulness (1-5)
- Hallucination flag (Y/N)
Will map thresholds per critical intent (90% correctness for order-status, 80% for refund-policy).

Jordan Lee: One enterprise blocker to surface: legal will likely ask for data processing addendum + right to audit. If they push for on-prem, we should have Private deployment checklist ready.

Maya Patel: Noted. I'll include that on the kickoff agenda. Thanks team — I'll schedule kickoff and post the calendar invite. :calendar: 

Samir Gupta: Posted initial spreadsheet draft: https://redwood.internal/sheets/novaretail-prompt-inventory (will update).

Riley Chen: I'll also add a small perf test plan: 1k concurrent warm tokens, KV cache priming scenario, and burst resilience.

Alyssa Morales: If legal wants encryption proofs, point them to our KMS integration docs and SOC2 report.

Maya Patel: Closing loop — deliverables list in thread: prompt inventory (Samir), eval set + rubric (Samir), cost/latency note + model recs (Riley), security Q responses (Alyssa). Thanks all.

Jordan Lee: :thumbsup:
